newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to sign Czech Republic plane-making pact.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to sign Czech Republic plane-making pact.

text.p: Taiwan's state-run Aerospace Industrial Development Corp said on Thursday it would sign an agreement on Saturday with Aero Vodochody of the Czech Republic to jointly manufacture small passenger airplanes.
The accord would begin Taiwan's first aerospace venture with any eastern European country, officials said.

"We will sign an agreement on Saturday with Aero Vodochody to jointly produce AE-270 commercial airplane. Before that, we cannot release any more details," a spokesman for the economics ministry-owned company told Reuters.
The local United Daily News said each side would take a 50 percent stake in the project and jointly invest more than US$60 million under the deal.

Aerospace Industrial Development would assemble the 10-seat turbine-propelled planes in Taiwan for sales in Asia-Pacific, while Aero Vodochody would assemble them in the Czech Republic for sales in eastern Europe, the paper said.

Last November, the economics ministry's Committee for Aviation and Space Industry Development said the ministry was considering a deal to jointly manufacture small passenger aircraft with Czech firms Aero Vodochody and LET G.S.
The Taiwan company's spokesman declined to comment on whether it was still talking with LET.
Aerospace Industrial Development, long a non-commercial military plane manufacturing centre, was converted into a state-run company in July 1996.
